anomalies.observed: Q5's source (pin 2) is on the system +5V rail, while its drain (pin 3) is on NET0192, the USB-C VBUS net. U42's VIN pin is also on NET0192 and SENSE is on +5V. The PMOS is therefore oriented opposite the usual LTC4412 ideal-diode input-to-load arrangement.
anomalies.expected: For the intended USB input ideal-diode path, Q5 should have its source toward USB VBUS (U42 VIN) and its drain toward the +5V load rail (U42 SENSE), providing forward input power and reverse-current blocking.

evidence.quote: "USB power-path controller intended to OR/protect a USB power input"

anomalies.impact: The reversed external PMOS can prevent the USB input from correctly feeding the system rail and undermines reverse-current blocking; the intended USB power-path behavior may fail or allow the system rail to backfeed USB VBUS.

anomalies.observed: Both ground pins of each isolated CAN transceiver are tied to the same GND net: U18 GND1/GND2 and U48 GND1/GND2.
anomalies.expected: The logic-side and bus-side grounds of each isolated CAN interface should remain galvanically separate for the specified isolated CAN buses.
anomalies.impact: Connecting both sides of each isolation barrier to the same ground defeats galvanic isolation, allowing ground-potential differences and common-mode disturbances on the CAN cabling to couple into the motherboard.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows two supported deviations: the USB ideal-diode PMOS is oriented opposite the input-to-load path, and both CAN transceivers have their isolated-side grounds tied to logic ground. These compromise the intended USB power protection and CAN galvanic isolation.
